usage: Painting pictures and also painting walls (for walls 'imbiancare' or 'tinteggiare' are more precise). Irregular: passato remoto dipinsi, participio dipinto (ho dipinto).

examples.en: He paints pictures in his free time.

examples.it: Abbiamo dipinto le pareti di verde.
examples.en: We painted the walls green.

examples.it: Vorrei che dipingesse il mio ritratto.
examples.en: I would like her to paint my portrait.

usage: Reflexive verb for shaving oneself; 'farsi la barba' is an everyday alternative. Irregular: passato remoto rasi, participio raso (mi sono raso). Takes essere.

examples.en: I shave every morning.

examples.it: Non si è raso per una settimana.
examples.en: He didn't shave for a week.
Will you shave for the wedding?

usage: Drying dishes, clothes or hair; the reflexive 'asciugarsi' is used with body parts (asciugarsi i capelli). Spelling change: an h is added before e/i (asciughi, asciugherò). Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Asciugo i piatti mentre tu lavi.
examples.en: I dry the dishes while you wash.
Did you dry your hair?

examples.it: Il sole asciugherà i vestiti in un'ora.
examples.en: The sun will dry the clothes in an hour.

usage: The opposite of 'vestirsi'. Reflexive, takes essere; the non-reflexive 'spogliare' means to undress someone else. Regular -are verb: mi spoglio, ti spogli.

examples.it: Il bambino si spoglia da solo.
examples.en: The child undresses by himself.

examples.it: Si è spogliato ed è entrato in acqua.
examples.en: He undressed and went into the water.
Get undressed and put on your pyjamas.

usage: Reflexive verb of summer holidays; the adjective 'abbronzato' means tanned. Do not confuse with 'scottarsi' (to get sunburnt). Takes essere. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: I tan easily.
You have got such a tan!

examples.it: Se resterai al sole senza crema, non ti abbronzerai, ti scotterai.
examples.en: If you stay in the sun without sunscreen, you won't tan, you'll get burnt.

usage: Transitive: to make something dirty; the reflexive 'sporcarsi' means to get dirty, with the stain introduced by 'di' (sporcarsi di sugo). Spelling change: h before e/i (sporchi, sporcherò). Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Non sporcare il pavimento con le scarpe!
examples.en: Don't dirty the floor with your shoes!

examples.it: Mi sono sporcato la camicia di sugo.
examples.en: I got sauce on my shirt.

examples.it: Se giocherai nel fango, sporcherai tutto.
examples.en: If you play in the mud, you'll get everything dirty.

en: to catch a cold; to get cold
usage: Two meanings: a person catches a cold (mi sono raffreddato) or food and objects cool down (la minestra si raffredda). The illness is 'il raffreddore'. Reflexive, takes essere. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: In winter I often catch a cold.

examples.it: Mi sono raffreddato la settimana scorsa.
examples.en: I caught a cold last week.

examples.it: Mangia, altrimenti la minestra si raffredderà.
examples.en: Eat, otherwise the soup will get cold.

usage: Intransitive, takes avere. The subject is usually the body part (il dito sanguina) or the person with 'dal naso'. Regular -are verb; the noun is 'il sangue'.

examples.en: The finger is still bleeding.

examples.it: Mi ha sanguinato il naso tutta la notte.
examples.en: My nose bled all night.

examples.it: Se sanguinasse ancora, dovremmo andare al pronto soccorso.
examples.en: If it were still bleeding, we would have to go to A&E.

usage: 'Soffrire di' is for illnesses (soffrire di mal di testa), 'soffrire per' for emotional causes; transitively with heat and cold (soffro il caldo). No -isc- (soffro, soffri); irregular participle sofferto.

examples.en: I suffer from the heat in summer.

examples.it: Ha sofferto molto per la fine della storia.
examples.en: He suffered a lot over the end of the relationship.
I don't want you to suffer.

usage: Intransitive verb of change of state, so it takes essere (è invecchiato). Also used of wine and cheese ageing. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: We all grow old.

examples.it: Mio padre è invecchiato molto negli ultimi anni.
examples.en: My father has aged a lot in the last few years.
We will grow old together.

usage: To move to a new home; the noun 'il trasloco' is equally common (fare il trasloco). 'Trasferirsi' is used for moving to another town. Spelling change: h before e/i (traslochi, traslocherò). Takes avere.

examples.en: We are moving house in June.

examples.it: Hanno traslocato in un appartamento più grande.
examples.en: They moved into a bigger flat.

examples.it: Traslocherò da solo con un furgone.
examples.en: I will move by myself with a van.

usage: Used for planes landing; the opposite is 'decollare'. Normally takes essere (l'aereo è atterrato), though avere is also accepted. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: The plane lands at ten.

examples.it: Siamo atterrati con mezz'ora di ritardo.
examples.en: We landed half an hour late.

examples.it: Atterreremo a Fiumicino tra venti minuti.
examples.en: We will land at Fiumicino in twenty minutes.

usage: Used for planes taking off; the opposite is 'atterrare'. Usually takes essere (l'aereo è decollato), avere is also possible. Also figurative: a project or career 'decolla'. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: The flight takes off at seven.
The plane took off on time.
We will take off as soon as it stops snowing.

usage: Reflexive form of 'perdere': to lose one's way. With an object it means to miss out on something (perdersi un film). Irregular participle perso (mi sono perso); passato remoto persi. Takes essere.

examples.it: Mi perdo sempre in questa città.
examples.en: I always get lost in this city.

examples.it: Ci siamo persi nel centro storico.
examples.en: We got lost in the old town.

examples.it: Con il navigatore non ti perderai.
examples.en: With the sat nav you won't get lost.

usage: Verb of movement, takes essere (sono scivolato). Impersonal 'si scivola' warns that a surface is slippery. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: Careful, it's slippery!
I slipped on the ice.
Without the right shoes you will slip.

usage: Throwing a ball or an object with force; also launching a product or campaign. Regular -are verb; the i is dropped before e/i (lanci, lancerò).

examples.en: Throw the ball to the dog!

examples.it: Ha lanciato il sasso nel lago.
examples.en: He threw the stone into the lake.

examples.it: Lancerà il pallone e tu lo prenderai.
examples.en: He will throw the ball and you will catch it.

usage: The opposite of 'alzare': volume, prices, heating, blinds and the voice. The reflexive 'abbassarsi' means to bend down or, of prices and temperatures, to drop. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: Turn the music down, please.
They lowered the prices.
If you turned down the heating, you would save money.

usage: Putting a room or a desk back in order; 'mettere in ordine' is a common alternative. Regular -are verb, takes avere.

examples.en: I tidy my room every Saturday.
Have you tidied the desk?

examples.it: Riordineremo tutto prima che arrivino gli ospiti.
examples.en: We will tidy everything before the guests arrive.

usage: The opposite of 'apparecchiare'; often used without an object ('Chi sparecchia?'). Regular -are verb, takes avere.

examples.en: Who is clearing the table tonight?

examples.it: Ho sparecchiato e ho lavato i piatti.
examples.en: I cleared the table and washed the dishes.
I will clear the table, you rest.

usage: Heating food, water or a room; 'riscaldare' is a synonym. The reflexive 'scaldarsi' means to warm oneself up or, of a person, to get worked up. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Scaldo il latte per il bambino.
examples.en: I am heating the milk for the baby.

examples.it: Ho scaldato la pizza nel forno.
examples.en: I heated the pizza in the oven.
The sun will warm the room.

usage: Adding oil, salt, sauce or dressing; the ingredient is introduced by 'con'. Takes -isc- in the present (condisco, condisci). Regular -ire verb; the noun is 'il condimento'.

examples.it: Condisco l'insalata con olio e limone.
examples.en: I dress the salad with oil and lemon.
Have you put the sauce on the pasta?

examples.it: Condiremo il riso con un po' di burro.
examples.en: We will season the rice with a little butter.

usage: Recycling paper, glass and plastic; the noun is 'il riciclo' or 'la raccolta differenziata' for separated waste collection. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Ricicliamo la carta e il vetro.
examples.en: We recycle paper and glass.

examples.it: Hanno riciclato le bottiglie di plastica.
examples.en: They recycled the plastic bottles.

examples.it: Se ricicleremo di più, inquineremo di meno.
examples.en: If we recycle more, we will pollute less.

usage: Planting trees, flowers and vegetables. Colloquially also 'to dump someone' (piantare il fidanzato) and 'piantare un chiodo' (to hammer in a nail). Regular -are verb.

examples.en: In spring I plant tomatoes.

examples.it: Abbiamo piantato un albero in giardino.
examples.en: We planted a tree in the garden.

examples.it: Pianterò le rose vicino al muro.
examples.en: I will plant the roses near the wall.

usage: Growing crops, vegetables or a garden; figuratively, cultivating an interest or a friendship. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: My uncle grows olives.
He tended the vegetable garden for years.

examples.it: Coltiverei un giardino se avessi spazio.
examples.en: I would grow a garden if I had the space.

usage: Reflexive verb for training in a sport or working out at the gym; the non-reflexive 'allenare' means to coach someone. Takes essere. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Mi alleno tre volte a settimana.
examples.en: I train three times a week.

examples.it: Si è allenata duramente per la gara.
examples.en: She trained hard for the race.
We will train together tomorrow.

en: to support (a team); to root for
usage: Being a fan of a team: 'tifare per la Juventus' or simply 'tifare Juventus'. The fan is 'il tifoso'. Regular -are verb, takes avere.

examples.en: I support Roma.

examples.it: Abbiamo tifato per l'Italia tutta la sera.
examples.en: We rooted for Italy all evening.
Who will you support on Sunday?

usage: In sport, to finish level; the result is 'il pareggio'. Also to even things out (pareggiare i conti). Regular -are verb; the i is dropped before e/i (pareggi, pareggerò).

examples.en: The two teams often draw.

examples.it: Ieri l'Italia ha pareggiato uno a uno.
examples.en: Yesterday Italy drew one all.
If they draw, they will go to penalties.

en: to score; to mark; to note down
usage: In sport, to score (segnare un gol); in everyday life, to write something down (segnare un numero) or mark something. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: Who scored?

examples.it: Segna il mio numero sul telefono.
examples.en: Put my number in your phone.

examples.it: Segnerà di sicuro, è il migliore.
examples.en: He will score for sure, he is the best.

usage: Practising a skill, a language or an instrument; the activity is introduced by 'in' or 'a' + infinitive. Reflexive, takes essere. Regular -are verb; the noun is 'l'esercizio'.

examples.it: Mi esercito ogni giorno con la pronuncia.
examples.en: I practise my pronunciation every day.
Have you practised enough?

examples.it: Esercitati a parlare con gli italiani.
examples.en: Practise speaking with Italians.

usage: Refers to a university degree only; the subject is introduced by 'in' (laurearsi in medicina). School graduation is 'diplomarsi'. Reflexive, takes essere; regular -are verb.

examples.en: I graduate in July.
She graduated in medicine.
When you graduate, we will celebrate.

en: to start again; to begin again
usage: Like 'cominciare', it takes avere with an object (ho ricominciato il lavoro) and essere when the subject is the thing that starts (la scuola è ricominciata). With a verb: 'ricominciare a' + infinitive. The i is dropped before e/i (ricominci, ricomincerò).

examples.en: Let's start again from the beginning.
School started again on Monday.
I have started running again.

usage: Intransitive with 'con' (comunicare con i colleghi); transitive in the sense of officially informing someone of something. Spelling change: h before e/i (comunichi, comunicherò). Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Comunico con i colleghi via email.
examples.en: I communicate with my colleagues by email.

examples.it: Ci hanno comunicato la data dell'esame.
examples.en: They informed us of the exam date.
We will announce the result tomorrow.

usage: The person can be the direct object: ti perdono. When the fault is named, it is the direct object and a introduces the person: perdonare un errore a qualcuno; gli ho perdonato tutto. Perdonami and mi perdoni can be apologies. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Ti perdono, ma non farlo più.
examples.en: I forgive you, but don't do it again.

examples.it: Non le ha mai perdonato quella bugia.
examples.en: He never forgave her that lie.
I hope you forgive me.

en: to pray; to beg; to ask (politely)
usage: Religious praying (pregare per qualcuno) and polite or urgent requests: 'ti prego' (please, I beg you), 'La prego di attendere'. The reply 'prego' (you're welcome) comes from this verb. Spelling change: h before e/i (preghi, pregherò).

examples.en: Please, help me!

examples.it: Hanno pregato in chiesa per un'ora.
examples.en: They prayed in church for an hour.

examples.it: La pregherei di aspettare un momento.
examples.en: I would ask you to wait a moment.

usage: Mostly impersonal: 'non importa' (it doesn't matter), 'non mi importa' (I don't care), with essere in compound tenses. As a transitive trade verb (importare merci) it takes avere. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: It doesn't matter, it's fine like this.

examples.it: Non mi è importato del risultato.
examples.en: I didn't care about the result.

examples.it: A chi importerà tra dieci anni?
examples.en: Who will care in ten years?

usage: The victim is introduced by 'a': 'mi hanno rubato la bici' (they stole my bike). The thief is 'il ladro', the crime 'il furto'. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: They stole my bike!
The thief steals at night.

examples.it: Se rubasse ancora, finirebbe in prigione.
examples.en: If he stole again, he would end up in prison.

en: to withdraw; to collect; to pick up
usage: Withdrawing cash (ritirare soldi al bancomat) and collecting parcels, documents or clothes from the cleaner's. The reflexive 'ritirarsi' means to withdraw or retire from an activity. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: I withdraw money at the cash machine.

examples.it: Ho ritirato il pacco alla posta.
examples.en: I picked up the parcel at the post office.

examples.it: Ritirerò il vestito dalla lavanderia domani.
examples.en: I will collect the dress from the cleaner's tomorrow.

usage: Charging a battery or phone and topping up a prepaid SIM (ricaricare la scheda). The noun 'la ricarica' is used for both. Spelling change: h before e/i (ricarichi, ricaricherò).

examples.en: I need to charge my mobile.
Did you recharge the battery?

examples.it: Ricaricherò la scheda con dieci euro.
examples.en: I will top up the SIM with ten euros.

usage: The standard verb for returning a phone call: 'ti richiamo dopo'. Also means to recall or to reprimand in more formal contexts. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: I'll call you back in five minutes.
He called me back right away.

examples.it: Se non risponde, richiamerò più tardi.
examples.en: If he doesn't answer, I will call back later.

usage: Making photocopies of documents, common at work, at school and in public offices (fotocopiare la carta d'identità). Regular -are verb; the noun is 'la fotocopia'.

examples.en: I am photocopying the documents for enrolment.
I photocopied my identity card.
Would you photocopy this page for me?
